definitions.explanation: Describes something so outstanding that nothing else can compare to it. A literary and formal expression.

examples.japanese: {比類|ひるい}ない{美|うつく}しさだ。
{彼|かれ}の{技術|ぎじゅつ}は{比類|ひるい}ないものだった。
この{作品|さくひん}は{比類|ひるい}ない{完成度|かんせいど}を{誇|ほこ}り、{多|おお}くの{人々|ひとびと}を{魅了|みりょう}した。
examples.english: This work boasted unmatched perfection and captivated many people.

notes:
Composed of {比類|ひるい} (comparison, equal) + ない (not). Literally means "without equal" or "having no comparison." A formal, literary expression used to praise something of the highest caliber.

FORMS:
- Attributive: {比類|ひるい}ない + noun ({比類|ひるい}ない{才能|さいのう})
- Also written: {比類|ひるい}のない ({比類|ひるい}のない{作品|さくひん})

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {比類|ひるい}ない{美|うつく}しさ: incomparable beauty
- {比類|ひるい}ない{才能|さいのう}: unmatched talent
- {比類|ひるい}ない{完成度|かんせいど}: unparalleled perfection
- {比類|ひるい}のない{存在|そんざい}: a peerless existence

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {無比|むひ}の: matchless, peerless — similarly formal; often used as a modifier ({天下|てんか}{無比|むひ} = peerless under heaven)
- {類|るい}を{見|み}ない: unprecedented, unheard of — emphasizes rarity rather than superiority
- {唯一無二|ゆいいつむに}の: one and only, unique — emphasizes uniqueness rather than superiority

REGISTER:
Highly formal and literary. Used in written Japanese, speeches, and formal descriptions. In everyday conversation, {他|ほか}にはない or すごい would be preferred.

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {比類|ひるい}なくなかったら
